execute_code.condition: When using execute_code for multi-step tool logic that requires structured output
execute_code.recommendation: Use execute_code (not terminal) for Python with tool calls. Import from hermes_tools.

execute_code.condition: When writing long Python functions in execute_code
execute_code.recommendation: Break into smaller functions. Use write_file first, then import/execute.

execute_code.condition: When connecting to services from execute_code
execute_code.recommendation: Check if service is running (docker ps, ps aux). Verify port and URL.

terminal.condition: When calling terminal with large payloads
terminal.recommendation: Use pagination, reduce output size, or split into smaller calls [CAUTION: 70 failures recorded — verify applicability]
Verify path exists before directory navigation/creation. Use Path.home() not ~ in Python.

terminal.condition: When reading file contents via terminal
terminal.recommendation: Use read_file instead of cat/head/tail — it has pagination and line numbers. [CAUTION: 70 failures recorded — verify applicability]

web_extract.condition: When web_extract takes >5s on a URL
web_extract.recommendation: Use max_chars=3000 to limit response. For 403 errors, switch to web_research instead.

web_extract.condition: When fetching from restricted URLs with web_extract
web_extract.recommendation: Switch to web_research for the same topic. 403 = anti-bot protection, retrying won't help.

web_extract.condition: When parsing documents efficiently with OCR
web_extract.recommendation: AgenticOCR: Parse only what you need. Instead of full OCR on entire documents: (1) Identify target sections from layout analysis; (2) Parse only relevant sections; (3) Skip headers, footers, boilerplate. This reduces OCR cost by 60-80% while maintaining extraction accuracy for the target information.

web_research.condition: When searching the web for current information
web_research.recommendation: Web research optimization: (1) Use specific queries — broad queries return noise; (2) max_results=5 is usually sufficient; (3. Categories: general, science, it, news; (4) Returns titles, URLs, snippets; (5) For full content, use web_extract on promising URLs. Search first, extract second — saves time.

web_research.condition: When using AI-powered search for information retrieval
web_research.recommendation: AI Search paradigm: Traditional search is query → rank → retrieve. AI search adds understanding: (1) Query understanding — what does the user actually want?; (2) Multi-source retrieval — search across different data types; (3) Answer synthesis — combine results into coherent answer; (4) Citation — link claims to sources. AI search replaces 10 blue links with synthesized answers.

web_research.condition: When web_research finds relevant results for tool-use optimization
web_research.recommendation: Follow up with web_extract on the top 2 URLs, then use execute_code to synthesize findings into distilled tips. This triple (research→extract→synthesize) accounts for 80% of tip extraction workflows.

delegate_with_model.condition: When selecting models for cost-performance tradeoffs
delegate_with_model.recommendation: CASTER: Breaking cost-performance barrier in multi-agent systems. Route tasks by complexity: (1) Simple tasks (summarization, formatting) → cheapest model; (2) Medium tasks (analysis, coding) → mid-tier model; (3) Hard tasks (reasoning, debugging) → best model. This routing achieves 90% of top-model quality at 30% of cost.

delegate_with_model.condition: When delegating research tasks to models via delegate_with_model
delegate_with_model.recommendation: Free models (nemotron-free, qwen-coder-free, mimo-v2-pro) handle 80% of tasks. Only escalate to paid models when: (1) task requires complex reasoning >3 steps, (2) code generation >50 lines, (3) domain expertise needed. Always try free first.

delegate_with_model.condition: When routing agents based on learned skills
delegate_with_model.recommendation: SkillOrchestra: Learn fine-grained skills from execution experience. (1) Each agent develops skill profiles from past runs; (2) Router matches tasks to agents by skill profile; (3) Skills transfer across domains when decomposed into primitives. This outperforms end-to-end routing by learning transferable skills.

delegate_task.condition: When delegating a task to a subagent
delegate_task.recommendation: Keep parent context lean — delegate entire workflows, not individual steps. Sub-agent architecture shows >90% context token reduction when parent delegates full tasks vs micro-managing. The parent should orchestrate, not execute.

delegate_task.condition: When spawning subagents for parallel isolated work
delegate_task.recommendation: Subagent delegation: (1) Subagents have NO memory — pass ALL context via context parameter; (2. Subagents CANNOT call: delegate_task, clarify, memory, send_message, execute_code; (3) Each gets its own terminal session; (4) Results are always summaries — intermediate data doesn't pollute parent context; (5) Max 3 parallel tasks — more causes conflicts. Isolation = reliability.

delegate_task.condition: When coordinating multiple agents with self-evolving protocols
delegate_task.recommendation: SECP (Self-Evolving Coordination Protocol): Agents can evolve their own coordination protocols. (1) Start with basic rules; (2) Evaluate coordination outcomes; (3) Modify rules that lead to failures; (4) Reinforce rules that lead to successes. This produces task-specific protocols that outperform fixed coordination schemes.

delegate_parallel.condition: When using delegate_parallel for research tasks that requires structured output
delegate_parallel.recommendation: Give each parallel task a UNIQUE id and self-contained context. Subagents have ZERO shared memory — each must receive ALL information it needs independently. Missing context in one subagent corrupts its entire output.

delegate_parallel.condition: When identifying parallelizable subtasks for concurrent execution
delegate_parallel.recommendation: Parallel task identification: (1) Two subtasks are parallelizable if they share NO dependencies; (2) Read-only operations are always parallelizable; (3) Write operations to different resources are parallelizable; (4) When in doubt, serialize — correctness > speed; (5) Use the dependency graph to find the critical path and optimize it.

delegate_parallel.condition: When orchestrating multi-agent workflows as DAGs
delegate_parallel.recommendation: Model agentic workflows as DAGs: (1) Nodes = agent tasks; (2) Edges = data dependencies; (3) Parallel execution for independent nodes; (4) Sequential for dependent nodes. DAG-based orchestration naturally identifies parallelism opportunities and prevents deadlock.

read_file.condition: When read_file fails with 'file not found'
read_file.recommendation: Verify path with search_files first. Use Path.home() not ~. Check case sensitivity.
Use offset and limit parameters. Read in chunks of 200-500 lines. Don't read entire files.

read_file.condition: When reading files efficiently without overwhelming context
read_file.recommendation: File reading optimization: (1) ALWAYS use offset and limit for large files; (2) Read in chunks of 200-500 lines; (3) Use search_files first to find relevant sections; (4) 1-indexed line numbers — offset=1 starts from beginning; (5. Files over 100K chars are rejected — always paginate. Never cat an entire file.

write_file.condition: When using write_file for large or multi-part generated content
write_file.recommendation: Always verify the write succeeded by reading back the first and last few lines with read_file. write_file OVERWRITES completely — if content generation was truncated, the file will be corrupted without any error.

write_file.condition: When using write_file for: write: plugin.yaml that requires structured output
write_file.recommendation: write_file auto-creates parent directories — no need for mkdir first

write_file.condition: When writing files that will be read by other agents or processes
write_file.recommendation: File writing for agent consumption: (1) Include a header comment explaining the file's purpose; (2) Use consistent formatting — other agents parse more reliably; (3) Add section markers for long files; (4) Include metadata (author, date, version) when files are shared between agents; (5) Keep files under 500 lines — split if needed.

patch.condition: When making targeted edits to existing files
patch.recommendation: Use patch(mode='replace') with enough context lines for unique matching. Include 3+ surrounding lines.

patch.condition: When debugging code generated by AI agents
patch.recommendation: AI code debugging methodology: (1) Reproduce the error — run the failing test; (2) Read the error message carefully — 80% of fixes are obvious from the error; (3) Check the most recent change — errors usually come from latest edits; (4) Use binary search — comment out half the code, see if error persists; (5) Fix the root cause, not the symptom.

patch.condition: When patch fails to find the old_string in a file
patch.recommendation: Read the file first to get the EXACT text including whitespace. The fuzzy matcher handles minor differences but NOT structural changes. If the file was reformatted, the old_string may no longer match any variant.

search_files.condition: When searching file contents or finding files by name
search_files.recommendation: Search files mastery: (1) target='content' for regex inside files; (2) target='files' for glob patterns; (3. Use file_glob to filter by extension; (4) Use output_mode: 'content' (default), 'files_only', 'count'; (5) Ripgrep-backed — faster than grep/find/rg. This is the ONLY way to search files.

Codebase navigation strategy: (1) Start from entry points (main, index, app); (2) Follow the call graph from there; (3) Use grep/search to find specific patterns; (4) Read tests to understand expected behavior; (5) Check imports to understand dependencies. Don't read files top-to-bottom — navigate by purpose.

search_files.condition: When redefining retrieval evaluation for agent search tools
search_files.recommendation: LLM-era retrieval evaluation: Traditional metrics (MRR, NDCG) don't capture whether retrieved info was actually USEFUL. New evaluation: (1) Answer correctness — did the retrieved info lead to a correct answer?; (2) Citation accuracy — are cited sources actually relevant?; (3) Completeness — did retrieval cover all needed aspects?; (4) Efficiency — was the minimal retrieval sufficient?

memory.condition: When managing agent memory across sessions with growing state
memory.recommendation: Implement dual-layer memory: (1) Active layer — high-recency, high-frequency items with slow decay; (2) Archive layer — older items with faster decay. FadeMem shows this achieves 45% storage reduction while improving multi-hop reasoning. Use Ebbinghaus-inspired exponential decay modulated by access frequency.

memory.condition: When designing agent memory architectures for long-term use
memory.recommendation: Agent memory types (from 𝕋ℝ𝑀𝑒𝑚): (1) Semantic — facts and concepts (like our distilled tips); (2) Episodic — specific past experiences (like session logs); (3) Procedural — learned skills and workflows (like our skills). All three are needed. Semantic alone is insufficient — procedural memory lets agents improve HOW they do things, not just WHAT they know.

memory.condition: When designing multi-layer memory for long-term agent persistence
memory.recommendation: Multi-layered memory architecture: Layer 1 (Working) — current conversation, in-context; Layer 2 (Episodic) — specific past interactions, time-stamped; Layer 3 (Semantic) — generalized knowledge facts; Layer 4 (Procedural) — skills and tips. Bridge transient short-term with long-term semantic through episodic indexing.

session_search.condition: When retrieving episodic memory from past sessions
session_search.recommendation: Episodic memory is the missing piece: Semantic memory knows 'what', but episodic memory knows 'when and how'. For agents, store: (1) Task context — what was being done; (2) Outcome — success or failure; (3) User reaction — satisfaction signal; (4) Time context — when it happened. Retrieval should be relevance-ranked by task similarity.

session_search.condition: When searching conversation history for relevant past context
session_search.recommendation: Conversation history search: (1) Use broad keywords with OR for recall; (2) Narrow with AND for precision; (3) Search by tool name to find relevant interactions; (4) Check the last 3 sessions first — most relevant context is recent; (5) Save important findings to memory to avoid re-searching.

session_search.condition: When using recursive summarization for long-term memory
session_search.recommendation: Recursive summarization: For very long conversations: (1) Summarize every N messages; (2) Periodically summarize the summaries; (3) Keep the most recent messages in full. This creates a hierarchical memory: detailed recent → summarized mid-range → high-level long-term. Retrieval searches all levels.

skill_manage.condition: When designing reusable skills for agent systems
skill_manage.recommendation: 7 design patterns for agentic skills: (1) Metadata-driven disclosure — skills declare capabilities; (2) Code-as-skill — executable scripts; (3) Workflow enforcement — structured sequences; (4) Self-evolving libraries — auto-improve; (5) Hybrid NL+Code macros; (6) Meta-skills — skills about skills; (7) Plugin/marketplace distribution. Match pattern to use case.

skill_manage.condition: When building and managing agentic skills beyond simple tool use
skill_manage.recommendation: SoK: Agentic Skills — Skills go beyond tool use. Tool use = call an API. Skill = reusable workflow combining multiple tools with domain knowledge. Architecture: (1) Skill definition — trigger condition + steps + expected outcome; (2) Skill acquisition — learn from experience or instruction; (3) Skill execution — reliable multi-step workflow; (4) Skill transfer — apply to new domains.

skill_manage.condition: When managing skill security and trust
skill_manage.recommendation: ClawHavoc case study: 1,200 malicious skills infiltrated a marketplace, exfiltrating API keys and credentials. Apply trust tiers: (1) Verified — from trusted source; (2) Community — peer-reviewed; (3) Untrusted — sandbox only. Never execute untrusted skills with access to credentials or file system.

validate_output.condition: When validating delegation results before trusting them
validate_output.recommendation: Output validation: (1) ALWAYS validate after delegate_with_model; (2) Checks: hallucination signals, contradictions, confidence; (3) Returns 0-10 confidence score; (4) Issues found = specific problems to address; (5) Recommendation tells you what to do next. Unvalidated delegation results are dangerous — always verify.

validate_output.condition: When evaluating agent performance across diverse tasks
validate_output.recommendation: Apply the 5-level evaluation taxonomy: L1=Agentic Skills (tool use), L2=Domain-Agent (domain performance), L3=Cross-Model (model comparison), L4=Protocol-Centric (agent-environment interface), L5=General Agent (cross-domain adaptability). Most evaluations stop at L2.

validate_output.condition: When detecting hallucinations in LLM agent outputs
validate_output.recommendation: Hallucination detection best practices: (1) Cross-reference claims against multiple sources; (2) Check for internal contradictions within the output; (3) Verify specific numbers, dates, and names — these hallucinate most; (4) Look for hedging language ('might', 'possibly') as uncertainty signal; (5) Compare output consistency across paraphrases.

context.condition: When managing agent context window across long sessions
context.recommendation: By turn 30, input tokens per call can be 5-10x what they were at turn 1. Most of those tokens are stale. Implement aggressive context pruning after every 10 turns.

context.condition: When the agent context window is 50%+ full and approaching limits
context.recommendation: Aggressively compress completed work into summary lines. Keep only: (1) the current task, (2) the last tool result, (3) key decisions. Delete all intermediate reasoning that led to completed tasks. Think of it as garbage collection for context.

context.condition: When managing reasoning token costs in agent loops
context.recommendation: Use a Shifted Thinking Window approach: cap reasoning tokens per turn and strip think tags from context. Train the model to adapt reasoning depth to problem complexity — simple problems get minimal reasoning, complex ones get more. Z1 shows 70% token reduction with no quality loss.
